_comment: Tool-option catalogs surfaced by lib/recommend.sh. Update install_command + url when vendors change. Pricing fields are general-tier descriptions — agent should fact-check current pricing via WebFetch when the user asks.

cmp.name: OneTrust
cmp.pricing: Enterprise — quote-based; typical floor ~$1,500/mo for full Privacy + Consent suite
cmp.install_command: Sign up; copy the OneTrust SDK script tag into your page <head>
pros: Recognized as the enterprise default in IAB TCF + GPC + APAC frameworks
Cookie scanner, geo rules, audit logs included
Full Consent Mode v2 + Microsoft UET consent + Meta consent integrations
cons: Heaviest CMP; can add 100kB+ of script weight if not pruned
Cost overshoot for small/mid sites
Onboarding requires admin training

cmp.name: Cookiebot (by Usercentrics)
cmp.pricing: Free up to 100 sub-pages; Premium from ~$11/mo per domain (small) up to ~$100/mo (large)
cmp.install_command: Sign up; paste the Cookiebot CMP script as the FIRST <script> in <head>; keep auto-blocking enabled
pros: Built-in IAB TCF v2.2 + Consent Mode v2 + Google certified
cons: Auto-blocking can break edge cases (canvas trackers, async iframes); occasional manual exemption needed
Branding requires the Premium plan
recommended_for: teams that want a single vendor for both consent + cookie scan

cmp.name: CookieYes
cmp.pricing: Free up to 25,000 page views/mo; paid from ~$9/mo for Basic up to $39/mo for Ultimate
cmp.install_command: Sign up; install via the WordPress plugin or paste the script tag into <head> for non-WP
pros: GDPR + CCPA + Consent Mode v2 supported
cons: Less advanced rule editor than OneTrust / Cookiebot
TCF support requires the higher tier
recommended_for: anyone needing a free starter CMP that scales

cmp.name: Klaro!
cmp.install_command: npm install klaro; or self-host the standalone klaro.js + klaro.css. Configure services in JS.
cons: No managed cookie scanner — you maintain the service list
No built-in TCF or geo-rules
No support beyond GitHub issues
recommended_for: engineers comfortable maintaining their own CMP

cmp.name: Termly
cmp.pricing: Free for cookie consent banner; Solo from ~$15/mo, Teams from ~$25/mo for combined Privacy + Consent
cmp.install_command: Sign up; embed the Termly CMP script in <head>; generates Privacy Policy + Terms in the same flow
pros: Combines policy generator with CMP — one bill
cons: Less granular than OneTrust
Branded banner on the free tier
recommended_for: small business owners who need legal + consent in one tool
marketing-led teams without a privacy engineer

cmp.name: Osano
cmp.pricing: Free up to 5k visitors/mo; paid from ~$199/mo for Business
cmp.install_command: Sign up; embed the Osano script in <head>; configure consent categories in the dashboard
cons: Mid-market price floor jumps quickly
Heavier than Cookiebot for similar features
recommended_for: B2B SaaS with US-state law scope (CO, CT, VA, etc.)

gtm-server.name: Google Cloud App Engine
gtm-server.pricing: Pay-per-use; budget ~$40-120/mo for a small to mid traffic site (F1 → F4 instance class)
gtm-server.install_command: Run Google's deployment script in Cloud Shell — provisions App Engine + GTM container
pros: Same auth surface as your other GCP usage
cons: GCP billing setup required
Cold starts on F1 — bump instance class for production
recommended_for: advertisers running heavy Google Ads + GA4 setups

gtm-server.name: Cloudflare Workers (custom)
gtm-server.pricing: Free tier covers ~100k requests/day; Workers Paid $5/mo for 10M; sgtm container itself runs on Workers via cf-sgtm or rolling-your-own adapter
gtm-server.install_command: Deploy a community sgtm-on-Workers template via wrangler; set GTM container ID + preview URL as secrets
pros: Edge-local; lowest tracking latency for global traffic
Same domain as the site (no third-party cookie issues)
cons: Community-maintained, not Google-supported — verify each Workers update against the GTM tag template you use
Some tags depend on GTM features not yet ported to Workers
recommended_for: high-volume sites where App Engine bills hurt

gtm-server.name: Stape.io
gtm-server.pricing: Free starter; paid from ~$20/mo (Basic) up to ~$300/mo (Custom) by traffic + features
gtm-server.install_command: Sign up; paste your GTM container ID; Stape provisions the sGTM endpoint and DNS
pros: Pre-built Stape Power-Ups for Meta CAPI, TikTok Events, etc.
cons: Vendor lock-in; you don't own the container host
Cost grows fast at high request volumes
recommended_for: small/mid teams without a DevOps function

gtm-server.name: Vercel (custom function)
gtm-server.pricing: Hobby + Pro tiers; sgtm requires Pro for production traffic; ~$20/mo Pro + function compute
gtm-server.install_command: Custom — deploy the Google sGTM container on Vercel as a long-running function (more friction than App Engine)
pros: Same vendor as the marketing site for many teams
cons: Not a first-class sGTM target; you maintain the bridge
Function timeouts can clip slow tag fires
recommended_for: Vercel-native stacks where ops simplification > raw compatibility

gtm-server.name: AWS App Runner
gtm-server.install_command: Push the sgtm container image to ECR, then create an App Runner service pointing at it
pros: Container-native; same image App Engine uses
cons: More setup than App Engine; no Google-published deployment script
VPC + IAM setup if you want private networking
recommended_for: teams that want ECS-class control without the EKS complexity

node.name: google-ads-api (NPM)
cons: Wraps the full Ads API; heavier than Measurement Protocol alone
recommended_for: Google Ads Enhanced Conversions, offline conversions, audience uploads

node.name: @google-analytics/data (NPM)
cons: Read-only — for sending events use Measurement Protocol via plain fetch

python.name: google-ads (PyPI)
cons: Larger dependency footprint

python.name: google-analytics-data (PyPI)
cons: Read-only

node.name: facebook-nodejs-business-sdk
cons: Heavy package; consider direct fetch + crypto for simple use cases

python.name: facebook_business (PyPI)
cons: Older API style

node.name: Bing Ads SDK for JS (community)
cons: No first-party Node SDK; offline conversions usually done via CSV upload to UI
recommended_for: UET offline conversion uploads when you have a server-side store

python.name: bingads (PyPI)
cons: SOAP-based

node.name: Direct fetch + REST
node.install_command: Use built-in fetch; no SDK published
cons: You write the HMAC + retry logic yourself

python.name: linkedin-api-python-client (community)
cons: Coverage focused on UGC/Profile; CAPI is direct REST
recommended_for: LinkedIn Marketing API; CAPI you'll likely call directly

node.name: Direct fetch
cons: You handle hashing + signing

python.name: Direct requests
cons: Manual hashing

node.name: twitter-api-v2
cons: Ads-API features are partial; check coverage before relying
recommended_for: X Ads CAPI calls + general X API

python.name: tweepy
cons: Ads coverage limited
recommended_for: general X API; Ads-CAPI direct fetch

node.name: Direct fetch
cons: Hash + sign yourself

python.name: Direct requests
cons: Manual hashing

node.name: Direct fetch
cons: Manual auth

python.name: Direct requests
cons: Manual auth

node.name: Direct fetch
cons: Manual hashing

python.name: Direct requests
cons: Manual hashing

node.name: jose (JWT signing)
cons: Apple's auth flow is JWT-then-token-exchange; you wire the rest
recommended_for: Apple Search Ads API JWT auth

python.name: PyJWT + cryptography
cons: Token-exchange step is your code
recommended_for: Apple Search Ads API JWT auth

lighthouse-runner.name: lighthouse CLI (local)
pros: Runs in CI without external service
cons: Single-machine results vary; aggregate with multiple runs
Doesn't capture field data — pair with CrUX / RUM for real users

lighthouse-runner.name: Lighthouse CI Server (self-hosted)
lighthouse-runner.install_command: Deploy lhci-server via Docker or Heroku-style host; @lhci/cli in CI uploads runs to it
cons: You maintain the host
No field-data aggregation
recommended_for: teams with budget for the host but no budget for SaaS

lighthouse-runner.name: Calibre
lighthouse-runner.install_command: Sign up; CLI: npm i -g @calibre/cli; calibre snapshot create
cons: Pricier than self-hosted
recommended_for: mid-market with performance as a KPI

lighthouse-runner.name: SpeedCurve
lighthouse-runner.install_command: Sign up; CLI for synthetic + LUX RUM beacon for field
cons: Premium pricing
Setup more involved than Calibre

lighthouse-runner.name: DebugBear
lighthouse-runner.install_command: Sign up; CLI for CI; pixel beacon for RUM
cons: Less flashy UI than SpeedCurve
recommended_for: small/mid teams who want SpeedCurve features at lower price

cwv-monitoring.name: web-vitals JS (DIY)
cwv-monitoring.install_command: npm i web-vitals; ship a small beacon to GA4 / your endpoint
cons: You own the dashboard / alerting
Sample-rate decisions are yours
recommended_for: everyone — start here, layer a paid tool only if dashboards are a bottleneck

cwv-monitoring.name: Vercel Speed Insights
cwv-monitoring.pricing: $10/mo per project (Pro tier required); higher for high-traffic
cons: Vercel-only
Aggregate dashboard; less drilldown than Calibre/SpeedCurve

cwv-monitoring.name: Cloudflare Web Analytics
cwv-monitoring.pricing: Free for sites on Cloudflare; included in Workers Paid
cwv-monitoring.install_command: Free + cookieless beacon — paste the snippet in <head> or use the Cloudflare zone setting
cons: Lighter dashboard than paid tools
Not as deep on INP attribution
recommended_for: Cloudflare-fronted sites that want privacy-first RUM

cwv-monitoring.name: Sentry Performance
cwv-monitoring.pricing: Performance Monitoring from ~$26/mo (Team) up; transactions priced per-volume
cons: Cost climbs with traffic
Heavier client JS than web-vitals alone
recommended_for: teams already on Sentry for errors

cwv-monitoring.name: Datadog RUM
pros: Single pane of glass with backend metrics
cons: Most expensive option at scale
Privacy review needed
recommended_for: enterprise on Datadog for everything else

listings.name: Google Business Profile
listings.install_command: Claim or create the profile at business.google.com; complete verification (video, phone, or postcard)
pros: Powers the local pack, Google Maps, and local answers in AI Overviews
Reviews, posts, Q&A, and messaging in one dashboard
Required for location assets in Google Ads / Performance Max
cons: Verification friction; suspensions common for virtual offices / service-area edge cases
Category and service-area rules are strict and opaque
recommended_for: any business with a storefront or service area
prerequisite for local extensions in Google Ads

listings.name: Apple Business Connect
listings.install_command: Sign in with an Apple ID at businessconnect.apple.com; claim the location and verify
pros: Controls how the business appears in Apple Maps, Siri, Spotlight, and CarPlay
Default map surface for iPhone users
cons: No native review ecosystem (pulls ratings from partners like Yelp)
Lower direct-search volume than Google

listings.name: Bing Places for Business
listings.install_command: Claim at bingplaces.com; fastest path is 'Import from Google Business Profile' and keep the sync enabled
pros: Feeds Bing local results AND the Bing index behind Microsoft Copilot and ChatGPT search — an AI-recommendation surface
One-click import + ongoing sync from Google Business Profile
Ties into Microsoft Advertising location assets
cons: Small direct-traffic share; easy to deprioritize and let go stale
Slower moderation than Google
recommended_for: goal: get recommended by AI assistants
anyone already maintaining a Google Business Profile (import takes minutes)

listings.name: Yelp for Business
listings.install_command: Search for the business at business.yelp.com and claim it; verify by phone or email
pros: Heavily cited by LLMs and AI assistants for 'best X near me' style queries
Large review corpus with high domain trust
Feeds ratings to Apple Maps and other partners
cons: Persistent ad-sales outreach after claiming
Review filter can hide legitimate reviews; no opt-out of the platform
recommended_for: goal: get recommended by AI assistants
restaurants, home services, local professional services
businesses with an active review-generation habit

listings.name: Better Business Bureau (BBB)
listings.pricing: Free business profile; accreditation is a separate paid program (varies by size, often $500+/yr)
listings.install_command: Search for the business on bbb.org and claim the free profile; accreditation is optional and separate
pros: High-trust domain that AI assistants cite for legitimacy / 'is X reputable' queries
Free profile includes ratings and complaint history transparency
Strong for service businesses selling trust
cons: Paid accreditation is often conflated with the free listing — you do not need to pay to be listed
Complaint handling obligations once engaged
recommended_for: goal: get recommended by AI assistants
established businesses with a clean track record

listings.name: Nextdoor for Business
listings.pricing: Free business page; local ads optional
listings.install_command: Claim the business page at business.nextdoor.com; verify the business address
pros: Neighborhood recommendation threads are literal word-of-mouth at scale
'Faves' and recommendations surface in neighbors' feeds
cons: Reach limited to claimed neighborhoods
Thin analytics; engagement varies widely by area
recommended_for: businesses whose customers are within a few miles

listings.name: Facebook Business Page
listings.install_command: Create the Page from a personal profile; complete the About, category, service area, and contact fields
pros: Recommendations posts in local groups drive word-of-mouth discovery
Prerequisite for running Meta ads later (Page + Business Manager)
Messaging + reviews + events in one place
cons: Organic reach for Pages is low without group activity or ads
Page management UX churns frequently
recommended_for: any business that may run Meta ads later

listings.name: Alignable
listings.install_command: Create a business profile at alignable.com; join local groups and ask/answer referral threads
pros: B2B referral network of small-business owners — built for passing word-of-mouth leads
Local groups and 'who do you recommend' threads
Free tier is enough to be findable
cons: Little consumer visibility — this is owner-to-owner networking
Value depends on active participation, not just claiming

listings.name: Angi
listings.pricing: Free listing; leads are pay-per-lead via Angi Ads / Angi Leads
listings.install_command: Search for the business on angi.com and claim it via the Angi for Pros flow; keep the free profile even if declining paid leads
pros: Large homeowner audience searching by trade
Free profile carries reviews and licensing info
AI assistants cite it for contractor-selection queries
cons: Aggressive lead-sales motion; shared leads can be low quality
Pay-per-lead costs escalate quickly if left unmanaged
recommended_for: trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, roofing, remodel
claim the free profile even if you never buy leads

listings.name: Houzz
listings.pricing: Free professional profile; Houzz Pro subscription optional
listings.install_command: Create a professional profile at houzz.com/pro; upload project photos — portfolio depth drives ranking
pros: Design-intent audience (kitchen/bath/remodel) with long project budgets
Portfolio + reviews format suits visual trades
cons: Skews design/remodel; weak for repair-type trades
Pro subscription upsell is persistent

listings.name: Thumbtack
listings.pricing: Free profile; pay-per-lead when customers contact you
listings.install_command: Sign up at thumbtack.com/pro; set services + travel area; profile is free until you respond to leads
pros: High-intent quote requests across hundreds of service categories
Free profile ranks in Thumbtack's own SEO-heavy category pages
cons: Lead prices fluctuate; charged per contact, not per job won
Race-to-respond dynamics favor fast repliers
recommended_for: solo operators and small crews wanting inbound quote requests
